**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/06/16 (Fri) 23:01
- [USER] User asked, "who makes the rules?"
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The rules that FINRA enforces are made by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), which is a government agency.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The SEC is responsible for overseeing the securities industry, which includes stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and other investment products.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] FINRA works closely with the SEC to create and enforce rules that protect investors and maintain the integrity of the financial industry.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] FINRA has the authority to create its own rules and regulations that govern the conduct of its member firms and their employees, as long as those rules do not conflict with SEC regulations.
- [USER] User asked, "how does FINRA make sure firms are honest?"
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] FINRA makes sure that financial firms are honest by conducting regular examinations and investigations of the firms it regulates.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] During these examinations, FINRA looks at a firm's books and records, as well as its business practices, to make sure the firm is following all of the rules and regulations that apply to its business.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] FINRA may also interview employees of the firm to ensure that they are knowledgeable about the products and services they offer, and that they are following the firm's policies and procedures.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] If FINRA finds that a firm has violated any rules or regulations, it has the authority to impose fines, suspend or expel the firm from the industry, or take other corrective action as necessary.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In addition to conducting examinations and investigations, FINRA also requires its member firms to disclose certain information to their customers, such as the risks associated with different investment products and the fees and expenses that customers will be charged.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] This helps ensure that customers have the information they need to make informed decisions about their investments.
